towns.name: Taos
towns.intro: Taos homes range from century-old adobe to new builds on the mesa. Most of what goes wrong here starts on the roof or in a crawlspace, and it starts quietly.
watchFor: Ponding on flat adobe roofs and blocked canales after snowmelt
Frozen pipes in crawlspaces and uninsulated portal walls
Wind damage to stucco, flashing and skylights
Rodents moving indoors when the weather turns

towns.name: Arroyo Seco
towns.intro: Arroyo Seco sits between the valley and the ski road, with older homes on wells and septic and long gravel drives that drift shut in winter.
watchFor: Well pumps and pressure tanks failing while no one is home
Septic and propane levels before a long absence
Snow drifting across driveways and gates
Pack rats in garages and outbuildings

towns.name: Taos Ski Valley
towns.intro: At over 9,000 feet, homes in the Ski Valley carry heavy snow for months. A missed check here can mean a collapsed deck or a burst line under three feet of powder.
watchFor: Snow load on roofs, decks and balconies
Ice dams and water working under shingles
Heat failures during deep cold snaps
Blocked vents on furnaces and water heaters

towns.name: Questa
towns.intro: Questa's quieter properties often sit far from neighbors, so problems can go unnoticed for weeks without a regular visit.
watchFor: Break-ins and trespassing on remote parcels
Wind-driven damage to roofs and outbuildings
Frozen exterior spigots and irrigation lines
Wildlife getting into crawlspaces

towns.name: Red River
towns.intro: Red River's cabins and condos fill up in ski season and summer, then sit empty in between. That gap is when pipes freeze and roofs leak.
watchFor: Frozen pipes in cabins left on low heat
Snow load on cabin roofs and decks
Spring runoff and river flooding near low-lying lots
Bears and rodents around trash and food storage

towns.name: Eagle Nest
towns.intro: Eagle Nest homes face the lake and the wind. Long, cold winters and open exposure make regular exterior checks especially important.
watchFor: Wind damage to siding, roofing and fences
Deep freezes and power outages
Ice and snow blocking doors and garage entries
Moisture and mold in closed-up homes

towns.name: Angel Fire
towns.intro: Angel Fire has more second homes than full-time residents. Winters are long and cold at 8,400 feet, and HOA rules often expect an owner contact on call.
watchFor: Furnace and boiler failures in sub-zero nights
Frozen and burst pipes in empty homes
Snow load and ice dams on steep roofs
HOA notices, packages and deliveries piling up
